questions.question: The minimum age for contesting elections to the Lok Sabha is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**25 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lok Sabha**, or the **House of the People**, is the **Lower House** of India’s bicameral **Parliament**.
 
• As per **Article 84 (b)** of the **Constitution of India**, a person must be a **citizen of India** and not less than **25 years of age** to be eligible to contest elections for the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• This age requirement also applies to the **Legislative Assembly** (Vidhan Sabha) of various states across the country.
 
• The members of the **Lok Sabha** are elected through **Direct Elections** based on **Universal Adult Suffrage** for a normal term of **five years**.
 
• Apart from the age criteria, a candidate must be registered as an **elector** for any parliamentary constituency and must not hold any **office of profit** under the Government of India or the Government of any State.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Age Requirements for Other Offices:**

 
 
• **30 years:** This is the minimum age required to become a member of the **Rajya Sabha** (Council of States) and the **State Legislative Council** (Vidhan Parishad) as per **Article 84** and **Article 173** respectively.
 
• **35 years:** This age limit is mandatory for the posts of the **President of India** (Article 58), the **Vice-President of India** (Article 66), and the **Governor** of a State (Article 157).
 
• **21 years:** Following the **73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts**, the minimum age to contest elections for **Panchayats** and **Municipalities** is set at 21 years.
 
• **18 years:** This is the minimum age for **Voting** in India. The **61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988** reduced the voting age from **21 years** to **18 years** by amending **Article 326**.

questions.question: Which of the following union territory has a legislative assembly?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Puducherry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Puducherry** is a **Union Territory** that operates with a unique administrative structure including its own **Legislative Assembly** and **Council of Ministers**.
 
• The creation of a legislature for Puducherry was made possible by the **14th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1962**, which added **Article 239A** to the **Constitution of India**.
 
• The **Puducherry Legislative Assembly** comprises **33 members**, out of which **30 are directly elected** by the people and **3 are nominated** by the **Central Government**.
 
• While the **President of India** governs the territory through a **Lieutenant Governor**, the **Chief Minister** and the Council of Ministers handle the executive functions for subjects in the **State List** and **Concurrent List**, excluding certain reserved matters.
 
• This setup allows the territory to have a representative form of government, distinguishing it from most other Union Territories that are governed directly by the **Union Government**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Territories with Legislatures**:

 
 
• **Delhi**: Established as the **National Capital Territory (NCT)** with an assembly via the **69th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1991** (Article 239AA).
 
• **Jammu and Kashmir**: Created as a UT with a legislative assembly under the **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019**.
 
 
 
• **Union Territories without Legislatures**:
 
 
• **Chandigarh**: Serves as the joint capital of Punjab and Haryana; it is managed by an **Administrator**.
 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**: An archipelago in the Bay of Bengal governed by a **Lieutenant Governor** without a local assembly.
 
• **Lakshadweep**: India's smallest UT, located in the Arabian Sea, administered through an **Administrator** appointed by the President.
 
• **Ladakh**: Separated from J&K in 2019, it functions as a UT without a legislative body.

questions.question: The Vice President can resign by submitting a resignation to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Vice President of India** holds a constitutional office for a term of **five years** from the date on which they enter upon their office.
 
• According to **Article 67(a)** of the **Constitution of India**, the Vice President may, by writing under their hand addressed to the **President**, resign their office.
 
• The resignation is a voluntary act and becomes effective as soon as it is accepted by the **President of India**.
 
• This provision ensures a formal **constitutional protocol** where the second-highest constitutional authority reports their departure to the highest authority of the **Republic of India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vice President's Constitutional Role**:

 
 
• The Vice President serves as the **Ex-officio Chairman** of the **Rajya Sabha** (Council of States) as per **Article 64**.
 
• Under **Article 65**, the Vice President acts as the **President** during casual vacancies or the absence of the President.
 
• The **election** of the Vice President is conducted by an **Electoral College** consisting of members of both Houses of **Parliament**.
 
 
 
• **Other Resignation Hierarchies**:
 
 
• The **President** submits their resignation letter to the **Vice President**, creating a reciprocal constitutional arrangement.
 
• The **Speaker of Lok Sabha** resigns by writing to the **Deputy Speaker** of the Lok Sabha.
 
• The **Chief Justice of India** and other **Supreme Court Judges** address their resignation to the **President**.
 
• The **Prime Minister** and other **Union Ministers** submit their resignations directly to the **President**.

questions.question: What is the title of Amrita Pritam's autobiography?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rasidi Ticket**__.

• Her autobiography is titled **Rasidi Ticket** (translated as **The Revenue Stamp**), which was first published in **1976**.
 
• The title of the book originated from a comment by the famous writer **Khushwant Singh**, who suggested that her life story was so brief it could be written on the back of a **revenue stamp**.
 
• The book is an intensely personal and honest account of her life, detailing her experiences during the **Partition**, her literary struggles, and her relationships with the poet **Sahir Ludhianvi** and the artist **Imroz**.

• **Sunehade** (Messages):

questions.question: Which Indian agency is responsible for real-time Air Quality Index (AQI) monitoring in cities?

options.text: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central Pollution Control Board**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** is a statutory organization established in **September 1974** under the **Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974**.
 
• It was later entrusted with powers and functions under the **Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981**, making it the apex body for monitoring environmental quality in India.
 
• The **National Air Quality Index (AQI)** was launched by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change in **2014** to disseminate real-time information about air quality in an easily understandable format for the general public.
 
• CPCB operates the **Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring System (CAAQMS)**, which provides live data on pollutant concentrations across various cities.
 
• The **AQI** calculates a single value based on eight major pollutants: **Particulate Matter (PM10 and PM2.5)**, **Nitrogen Dioxide (NO2)**, **Sulphur Dioxide (SO2)**, **Carbon Monoxide (CO)**, **Ozone (O3)**, **Ammonia (NH3)**, and **Lead (Pb)**.
 
• Air quality is classified into six categories: **Good**, **Satisfactory**, **Moderately Polluted**, **Poor**, **Very Poor**, and **Severe**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog)**:

 
 
• Formed on **January 1, 2015**, it replaced the Planning Commission.
 
• It serves as the premier policy **think tank** of the Government of India, promoting **cooperative federalism**.
 
 
 
• **Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)**:
 
 
• Established in **1942**, it is one of the largest **research and development** (R&D) organizations in India.
 
• While it conducts research on environmental engineering through its lab **NEERI**, it is not the primary agency for regulatory real-time monitoring.
 
 
 
• **Sameer App**:
 
 
• An official mobile application developed by the **CPCB** that provides hourly updates of the **National Air Quality Index** and allows citizens to lodge complaints related to air pollution.

questions.question: The Air Quality Early Warning System is primarily designed to:

options.text: Alert citizens about upcoming high pollution days

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alert citizens about upcoming high pollution days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Air Quality Early Warning System (AQEWS)** is an integrated system designed to provide **advance information** about anticipated air quality deterioration, specifically in the **Delhi-NCR** region.
 
• Developed by the **Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM)**, Pune, the system uses complex mathematical models to predict **pollution levels** up to **72 hours** to **10 days** in advance.
 
• The primary objective is to facilitate **proactive decision-making** by authorities and allow **citizens** to take preventive health measures during periods of **extreme pollution**.
 
• It utilizes real-time data from **satellite observations**, including **Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD)** and **active fire counts**, to estimate the contribution of **stubble burning** to local air quality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The system is a crucial component of the **Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP)**, which dictates specific emergency measures like banning construction or vehicle entry based on **Air Quality Index (AQI)** forecasts.

 
 
• **Pollutants Tracked:** The system focuses heavily on **PM2.5**, **PM10**, and **Nitrogen Oxides (NOx)**, which are the primary drivers of respiratory ailments.
 
• **Regulatory Framework:** It works in coordination with the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** and the **Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM)**.
 
• **Technological Scope:** Unlike **industrial air filtration** which uses **Electrostatic Precipitators**, this is an **informatics tool** for monitoring and prediction rather than a mechanical cleaning device.
 
• **Alternative Monitoring:** Concepts like **soil contamination** or **water pollution** fall under different regulatory systems, such as the **National Water Quality Monitoring Programme**, and are not the focus of **AQEWS**.

• The tournament was organized by the **Badminton Association of India (BAI)** and took place from **August 14 to August 31, 2013**, featuring top-tier domestic and international talent.

• This signal is transmitted through the **Olfactory nerve (Cranial Nerve I)** directly to the **olfactory bulb** in the brain, which then processes the information to identify the scent.

questions.question: In a fixed exchange rate system, when some government action increases the exchange rate, this is called _______, making domestic currency cheaper.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**devaluation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Devaluation** refers to the deliberate downward adjustment of the value of a country's currency relative to another currency, a group of currencies, or a standard like **gold**. This policy tool is exclusively used within a **Fixed Exchange Rate System**.
 
• In this context, **increasing the exchange rate** means that more units of the domestic currency are required to purchase one unit of a foreign currency (e.g., shifting from 70 to 80 units of domestic currency per **USD**). This action directly makes the domestic currency **cheaper** or less valuable in the international market.
 
• The primary objective of **devaluation** is often to correct a **Balance of Payments (BoP)** deficit. By making domestic goods cheaper for foreign buyers, it encourages **Exports**, while making foreign goods more expensive for domestic consumers, thereby discouraging **Imports**.
 
• A significant historical instance occurred in **India** in **July 1991**, when the **Reserve Bank of India** devalued the **Rupee** by approximately **18-19 percent** in two steps to address a severe economic crisis and low foreign exchange reserves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revaluation**:

 
 
• This is the opposite of **devaluation** within a **fixed exchange rate system**. It involves an official upward adjustment of the currency value by the government or **Central Bank**, making the domestic currency stronger and foreign goods cheaper.
 
 
 
• **Depreciation and Appreciation**:
 
 
• **Depreciation** refers to a decrease in a currency's value caused by **market forces** (demand and supply) rather than government mandate. This occurs in a **Flexible (Floating) Exchange Rate System**.
 
• **Appreciation** refers to an increase in the currency's value due to market demand in a **floating system**.
 
 
 
• **Managed Floating System**:
 
 
• This is a hybrid system where the **exchange rate** is primarily determined by the market, but the **Central Bank** intervenes occasionally to stabilize or influence the rate, often referred to as a **dirty float**.

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **algebraic identity**: (a − b)² + 4ab = (a + b)²

Here, let **a = 412** and **b = 388**.

⇒ (412 + 388)² = (800)²

⇒ 640000

**∴ The correct answer is 640000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (412 − 388)² + 4 × 412 × 388

**Formula Used:** Expansion of **(a − b)²** and **(a + b)²**

⇒ (412 − 388) = 24

⇒ (24)² + 4 × 412 × 388

⇒ 576 + 639424

⇒ 640000

**∴ The correct answer is 640000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square of Sum

The identity for the square of a sum is **(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²**.

Square of Difference

The identity for the square of a difference is **(a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²**.

Relationship Identity

Combining the two provides the useful relation: **(a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab**.

questions.question: The perimeter of a rectangle is 48 cm. The length of the rectangle is 3 times of its breadth. What is the length (in cm) of its diagonal?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Ratio** of **Length** to **Breadth** be 3 : 1.

**Perimeter** ratio = 2 × (3 + 1) = 8 units = 48 cm.

1 unit = 6 cm ⇒ **Breadth** = 6 cm and **Length** = 18 cm.

**Diagonal** = √(18² + 6²) = 6 × √(3² + 1²) = 6√10 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 6√10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Perimeter** of **Rectangle** = 48 cm, **Length** (L) = 3 × **Breadth** (B).

**Formula Used:** **Perimeter** = 2(L + B) | **Diagonal** (d) = √(L² + B²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/37e4acf357bda1783d001a3173f8768074d9b927df2826476fab99d610cb303d.png] 

⇒ 2(L + B) = 48

⇒ L + B = 24

⇒ Substitute L = 3B: 3B + B = 24

⇒ 4B = 24 ⇒ B = 6 cm

⇒ L = 3 × 6 = 18 cm

⇒ **Diagonal** (d) = √(18² + 6²)

⇒ d = √(324 + 36) = √360

⇒ d = √(36 × 10) = 6√10 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 6√10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Rectangle

The total space occupied by a **Rectangle** is calculated as Area = **Length** × **Breadth**.

Pythagoras Theorem

For a **Right-angled Triangle** formed by the **Diagonal**, L² + B² = d².

Circumcircle of a Rectangle

The **Radius** of the circle passing through all four vertices of a **Rectangle** is half of its **Diagonal** (R = d/2).

questions.question: Average of 8 numbers is 57. Average of first 4 numbers is double of the average of last 4 numbers. What is the sum of the last 4 numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Average** of first 4 and last 4 numbers = 2 : 1.

Since the **count of numbers** is the same (4 each), the **Sum ratio** is also 2 : 1.

Total units for sum = 2 + 1 = 3 units.

Total **Sum** of 8 numbers = 8 × 57 = 456.

Sum of last 4 numbers (1 unit) = 456 ÷ 3 = 152.

**∴ The correct answer is 152.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average of 8 numbers = 57. Average of first 4 is double the average of the last 4.

**Formula Used:** Sum = Average × Number of observations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/78097e4054ebe2fafb4612048077a3c12a70041d98b92158cb054cd71de34089.png] 

⇒ Total **Sum** of all 8 numbers = 8 × 57 = 456.

⇒ Let the **average** of the last 4 numbers = x.

⇒ Average of the first 4 numbers = 2x.

⇒ **Sum** of first 4 numbers = 4 × 2x = 8x.

⇒ **Sum** of last 4 numbers = 4 × x = 4x.

⇒ Total sum = 8x + 4x = 12x.

⇒ 12x = 456.

⇒ x = 456 ÷ 12 = 38.

⇒ **Sum** of the last 4 numbers = 4x = 4 × 38 = 152.

**∴ The correct answer is 152.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When two groups are combined, the total average is calculated as A = (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Sum of Observations

The total sum is always the product of the **Arithmetic Mean** and the total number of items: Sum = Average × Count.

Equal Groups Property

If the number of items in two groups is equal, the **Combined Average** is simply the average of their individual averages: (a₁ + a₂) ÷ 2.

questions.question: The average of 17 consecutive natural numbers is A. What is the sum of the largest and the smallest numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any set of numbers in an **Arithmetic Progression** (like consecutive natural numbers), the **Average** is always equal to the **Arithmetic Mean** of the first and last terms.

Average (A) = (Smallest + Largest) ÷ 2

By cross-multiplying:

Sum of Smallest and Largest = 2 × Average = 2A

**∴ The correct answer is 2A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total numbers (n) = 17, **Average** of these consecutive numbers = A.

**Formula Used:** Average of an Arithmetic Progression (AP) = (a + l) ÷ 2, where 'a' is the first term and 'l' is the last term.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d439bc9ae56314878ca168c8cccec6d1f00be16bab3e45979cd9d5c4d70d7297.png] 

⇒ Let the 17 **consecutive natural numbers** be n₁, n₂, n₃, ..., n₁₇.

⇒ These numbers form an **Arithmetic Progression** with a common difference (d) = 1.

⇒ For any AP, the **Sum of all terms** = (n ÷ 2) × (First term + Last term).

⇒ Also, **Average** = Sum ÷ n.

⇒ Average (A) = [(n ÷ 2) × (n₁ + n₁₇)] ÷ n

⇒ A = (n₁ + n₁₇) ÷ 2

⇒ n₁ + n₁₇ = 2 × A = 2A

**∴ The correct answer is 2A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Middle Term Property

In an **Arithmetic Progression** with an odd number of terms (n), the **Average** is always the exact middle term, which is the ((n+1)/2)th term.

Sum of First 'n' Natural Numbers

The sum of the first 'n' natural numbers is calculated using the formula: Sₙ = n(n + 1) ÷ 2.

Average of Even and Odd Numbers

The average of the first 'n' consecutive **even** numbers is (n + 1), while the average of the first 'n' consecutive **odd** numbers is simply n.

questions.question: 210 chips and 294 toffees are to be distributed among maximum number of boys. Each boy gets the same number of chips. Each boy get the same number of toffees. How many chips does each boy get?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **maximum number of boys**, calculate the **HCF** of 210 and 294.

HCF(210, 294): 294 − 210 = 84. Factors of 84 are 42, 21, etc. Since 42 divides both, **HCF = 42**.

Number of chips per boy = Total chips ÷ HCF = 210 ÷ 42 = 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 chips.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total chips = 210, Total toffees = 294.

**Formula Used:** Maximum group size = HCF (Highest Common Factor); Items per person = Total items ÷ Group size.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1c70c62e2e64d191df6987bf37a23f10a00c8496b172aae9aff7d1dde4df3266.png] 

⇒ Prime factorization of 210 = 2 × 3 × 5 × 7

⇒ Prime factorization of 294 = 2 × 3 × 7 × 7

⇒ HCF (Maximum number of boys) = 2 × 3 × 7 = 42

⇒ Chips received by each boy = Total chips ÷ Total boys

⇒ Chips per boy = 210 ÷ 42 = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5 chips.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

HCF is the greatest number that divides two or more numbers without leaving a remainder. It is used to find the maximum possible size for equal distribution.

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

LCM is the smallest positive integer that is divisible by each of the given numbers. Relationship: Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM.

HCF by Difference Method

The HCF of two numbers is also a factor of their difference. This is a quick way to narrow down the HCF in exams.

Profit of **30%** implies that the **Selling Price (SP)** is **130%** of the **Cost Price (CP)**.

Ratio method: 30% = 3/10 ⇒ CP = 10 units, Profit = 3 units, SP = 13 units.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Selling Price (SP)** = ₹7540

**Profit Percentage** = 30%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = [Selling Price × 100] ÷ [100 + Profit %]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fc3df88f67b082857acda0f7ca69233ea3775350bf373751d5c53ea518297e45.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = [7540 × 100] ÷ [100 + 30]

Basic Profit and Loss Formulas

Selling Price Calculation

Marked Price and Discount

questions.question: The difference between cost price and selling price of an article is Rs. 120. Profit percentage is 30 percent. What is the selling price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **difference** between **Selling Price (SP)** and **Cost Price (CP)** is the **Profit**.

Given **Profit** = 30% of CP = ₹120.

⇒ 30% → 120

⇒ 1% → 4

**Selling Price** = 100% (CP) + 30% (Profit) = 130%.

⇒ 130 × 4 = ₹520.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹520.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Difference between CP and SP (Profit) = ₹120, Profit Percentage = 30%.

**Formula Used:** Profit = SP − CP; Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100; SP = CP + Profit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d266d82c70acd1ba9151c39acc9a5e2112f88f08724cc24ce4cc52d6396f8927.png] 

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** be ₹x.

⇒ Profit = 30% of x = 120

⇒ (30 ÷ 100) × x = 120

⇒ x = (120 × 100) ÷ 30

⇒ x = 4 × 100 = ₹400

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = CP + Profit

⇒ SP = 400 + 120

⇒ SP = ₹520

**∴ The correct answer is ₹520.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Fundamentals

Profit occurs when **SP > CP** and Loss occurs when **CP > SP**. Profit/Loss is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise.

Basic Formulas

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 | Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Finding CP from SP

CP = [100 ÷ (100 + Profit %)] × SP (for profit) or CP = [100 ÷ (100 − Loss %)] × SP (for loss).

questions.question: A pipe can empty 1/4 part of a tank in 8 minutes. In how much time (in minutes) can it empty 1/2 part of that tank?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Time** taken is directly proportional to the **volume** of the tank to be emptied.

1/4 part → 8 min

Multiply both sides by 2 to get 1/2 part:

(1/4 × 2) part → 8 × 2 min

1/2 part → 16 min

**∴ The correct answer is 16 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time to empty 1/4 part = 8 min

**Formula Used:**

Total Time = Time taken / Fraction of work done

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e1b8dbbc04143c2deb9bcc4edd5b4e4ba88ba30c0a29507d1d5e4f4b0ca24ca2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time to empty the **full tank** (1 part) = 8 × 4

⇒ Full tank time = 32 min

⇒ Time to empty **1/2 part** of the tank = 32 × (1/2)

⇒ Time = 16 min

**∴ The correct answer is 16 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unitary Method for Fractions

If 1/n part of a task is completed in 't' time, then the full task (1 unit) is completed in (n × t) time.

Pipes and Cisterns Efficiency

Efficiency of an emptying pipe is considered **negative** when working together with an inlet pipe in total work calculations.

Time and Work Relation

Work Done = Rate of Work × Time. For a constant rate, Work and Time are in **direct proportion**.

questions.question: Q and R together are 8 times as efficient as P. P and R together are 5 times as efficient as Q. P, Q and R together can complete a work in 10 days. Q alone can complete the same work in how many days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given **P + R = 5Q**. Adding **Q** to both sides: **P + Q + R = 6Q**.

This means the **Total Efficiency** of **P, Q, and R** combined is **6 times** the efficiency of **Q** alone.

Since **Time** is inversely proportional to **Efficiency**, **Q** will take 6 times as much time as the group.

Time taken by **Q** = 6 × 10 = 60 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 60 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **P, Q and R** together complete work in **10 days**.

Ratio of efficiencies: (Q + R) / P = 8 / 1 (Total units = 9) and (P + R) / Q = 5 / 1 (Total units = 6).

⇒ To equalize the total efficiency, take **LCM(9, 6) = 18**.

⇒ New Ratio 1 (multiply by 2): (Q + R) : P = 16 : 2.

⇒ New Ratio 2 (multiply by 3): (P + R) : Q = 15 : 3.

⇒ Thus, efficiency of **P = 2**, **Q = 3**, and **Total = 18**.

⇒ Time taken by **Q** alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of **Q** = 180 ÷ 3 = 60 days.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency (E) is inversely proportional to Time (T) for a constant amount of work: **E₁ × T₁ = E₂ × T₂**.

Combined Efficiency

When multiple people work together, their individual **Efficiencies** are added to find the **Total Efficiency** of the group.

Work-Wages Principle

Wages are generally distributed in the direct ratio of the **Work Done** or the ratio of **Efficiencies** (if time spent is same).

questions.question: Length of train A is 400 metres. Length of train B is 800 metres. Both the trains cross each other in 80 seconds. These trains are running in opposite direction. What is the total speed (in m/s) of A and B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two trains cross in **opposite direction**, their **Relative Speed** is the sum of their individual speeds.

**Relative Speed** = (Length of Train A + Length of Train B) ÷ Time

**Total Speed** = (400 + 800) ÷ 80 = 1200 ÷ 80 = 15 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 15 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Length of Train A** (LA) = 400 m

**Length of Train B** (LB) = 800 m

**Time taken to cross** (t) = 80 sec

**Formula Used:**

**Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)** = (LA + LB) ÷ t

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e5922957aad1f6a1b6465e3d411353587a3c5ed2393d6f3ee91e4ead756e185.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Distance** to be covered = 400 + 800 = 1200 m

⇒ **Relative Speed** = 1200 ÷ 80

⇒ **Relative Speed** = 15 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 15 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

If two trains of speeds SA and SB run in the **same direction**, the relative speed is |SA − SB|.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing a Stationary Point Object

When a train crosses a **pole or a man**, the distance covered is equal to the **length of the train** itself.

questions.question: A 400 metres long train crosses a man walking in opposite direction in 8 seconds. Speed of train is 4 times of the speed of man. What is the speed (in km/hr) of train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** = Distance ÷ Time = 400 ÷ 8 = 50 m/s.

Ratio of **Train speed** to **Man speed** = 4 : 1.

In **opposite direction**, relative units = 4 + 1 = 5 units.

5 units = 50 m/s ⇒ 1 unit = 10 m/s.

**Speed of train** = 4 units = 40 m/s = 40 × (18/5) = 144 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 144 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of **Train** (L) = 400 m

**Time** taken (t) = 8 seconds

**Speed of train** (Vₜ) = 4 × **Speed of man** (Vₘ)

**Formula used:**

Relative Speed = Total Distance ÷ Time

In **opposite direction**, Relative Speed = V₁ + V₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4789bf4352dde206a1da4a7cee3d112c6222b149d860b74faf12b094eaa4093b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 400 ÷ 8

⇒ Vₜ + Vₘ = 50 m/s

⇒ Since Vₜ = 4Vₘ, substituting the value:

⇒ 4Vₘ + Vₘ = 50

⇒ 5Vₘ = 50 ⇒ Vₘ = 10 m/s

⇒ Speed of train (Vₜ) = 4 × 10 = 40 m/s

⇒ Converting to **km/hr**: 40 × (18 ÷ 5)

⇒ 8 × 18 = 144 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 144 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Trains

When two objects move in **opposite directions**, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂. When they move in the **same direction**, Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|.

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5. To convert **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18.

Crossing a Point Object

When a train crosses a **man, pole, or tree**, the distance covered is equal to the **length of the train** itself.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
By next summer, the builders will have completed the tower.

options.text: The tower has been completed by the builders by next summer.
The tower will be completed by the builders by next summer.
The tower will have been completed by the builders by next summer.
The tower was completed by the builders by next summer.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The tower will have been completed by the builders by next summer**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The given sentence 'By next summer, the builders will have completed the tower' is in the **Active Voice** and follows the **Future Perfect Tense** structure.

• The active structure for this tense is: **Subject + will have + Past Participle (V3) + Object**. In this sentence, **the builders** is the subject, **will have completed** is the verb, and **the tower** is the object.

• To convert a **Future Perfect** sentence into **Passive Voice**, the structure used is: **New Subject (Object of active) + will have been + Past Participle (V3) + by + New Object (Subject of active)**.

• Following this rule, **the tower** moves to the subject position, the auxiliary verb becomes **will have been**, and the main verb **completed** remains in its **V3** form.

• The phrase **by next summer** is an **Adverbial of Time** indicating a deadline in the future, which remains unchanged in position or tense during the conversion.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Future Perfect Tense** (Passive):

• It emphasizes the **completion** of an action before a specific point in the future rather than the doer of the action.

• The inclusion of **been** is mandatory to distinguish the passive form from the active future perfect.

• Distinguishing other Tenses:

• **Simple Future Passive**: Uses **will be + V3** (e.g., 'The tower will be completed'). This lacks the 'completion by a deadline' nuance.

• **Present Perfect Passive**: Uses **has/have been + V3** (e.g., 'The tower has been completed'). This refers to an action already finished in the past with current relevance.

• **Simple Past Passive**: Uses **was/were + V3** (e.g., 'The tower was completed'). This indicates the action occurred at a specific time in the past.

</ul
